new.tovw: Lead grade D: a period local paper and a Duluth special report an old railroad hand's search with blueprints of the construction camps, but the camp is not identified and the gold rests on a death-bed story; no recovery reported.
new.n: Construction-camp gold on the Northern Pacific west of Wadena (Buchan's blueprints, 1905)
new.pl: Northern Pacific right of way west of Wadena, 'between this city and the junction'; camp site not identified (ring 5 km on the Wadena station)
new.st: In June 1905 J. Buchan, about 70, of Pine River, who had worked on the Northern Pacific construction when the road was built through Wadena, was searching for several thousand dollars in gold he said was buried at one of the construction-gang camps. He carried blueprints of the right of way marking the camp sites, given him by a friend on his death-bed. He first tried east of the town and failed, then placed the cache west of Wadena, between the town and the junction, while lodging at a farm three miles east of the village. Nothing is reported found. Pin is the Wadena station, not the camp.
new.t: Railroad right of way and private farmland: ask first. The MnDOT Northern Pacific valuation sheets (roll 1606C) and the 1870s construction-camp sites west of Wadena are the way to narrow it.
new.warn: Active railroad right of way and private land.
